questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The solution of the differential equation $(x+1) \frac{d y}{d x}-y=e^{3 x}(x+1)^2$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $\frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{y}{x+1}=e^{3 x}(x+1)$
Above is linear differential equation of form
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{d y}{d x}+P x=Q \\
& \therefore \quad \mathrm{IF}=e^{\int P d x}=e^{\int-\frac{1}{x+1} d x}=e^{-\ln (1+x)}=\frac{1}{1+x}
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow$ Solution will be
$\begin{aligned}
y \cdot \mathrm{IF} & =\int Q \cdot \mathrm{IF} d x \\
y \cdot \frac{1}{1+x} & =\int e^{3 x}(x+1) \times \frac{1}{(1+x)} d x \\
\frac{y}{1+x} & =\frac{e^{3 x}}{3}+C^{\prime} \\
\frac{3 y}{1+x} & =e^{3 x}+C^{\prime} \quad \quad\left[\because C=3 C^{\prime}\right]
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\frac{d y}{d x}-y \log _e 2=2^{\sin x}(\cos x-1) \log _e 2$, then $y$
questions.solution:
$\frac{d y}{d x}-y \log _e 2=2^{\sin x}(\cos x-1) \log _e 2$
This is linear differential equation
$\text{ I.F. }=e^{-\log _e 2 \int d x}=e^{-x \log _e 2}=2^{-x}$
then general Solution is
$y 2^{-x}=\int 2^{-x} 2^{\sin x}(\cos x-1) \log _e 2 d x+c$
Now let $\sin x-x=t \Rightarrow(\cos x-1) d x=d t\begin{aligned}
& \therefore y 2^{-x}=\log _e 2 \int 2^t d t+c \\
& \therefore y 2^{-x}=2^t+c \\
& \therefore y=2^{x+t}+c 2^x \\
& \therefore y=2^{\sin x}+c 2^x
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The number of solutions of $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y+1}{x-1}$, when $y(1)=2$ is
questions.solution:
Since, $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y+1}{x-1}$
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{y+1}=\frac{d x}{x-1}$
After integrating on both sides, we have
$\log (y+1)=\log (x-1)-\log C$
$C(y+1)=(x-1)$
$C=\frac{x-1}{y+1}$
If $x=1$, then $y=2$, so $C=0$
Therefore, $x-1=0$
Hence, there is only one solution.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right) \tan x=y \sec ^2 x+\sin x$, find general solution
questions.solution: Given that $\begin{aligned}& \left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right) \tan x=y \sec ^2 x+\sin x \\ & \tan x\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)- y \sec ^2 x=\sin x \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}+\left(\frac{-\sec ^2 x}{\tan x}\right) y=\frac{\sin x}{\tan x}\\ & \text{ Here, } P=-\frac{\sec ^2 x}{\tan x} \text{$ and $} Q=\cos x \\ & \text{ IF }= e^{\int P d x}=e^{\int \frac{-\sec ^ 2 x}{\tan x} d x} \\ & \text{ IF }= e^{-\log(\tan x)}=e^{\log \cot x}=\cot x \\ & \text{ Now, } y \times \mathrm{IF}=\int( Q \times \mathrm{IF}) d x+C \\ & y \cdot \cot x=\int \cos x \cdot \cot x+C \\ & y \cdot \cot x=\int \frac{1-\sin ^2 x}{\sin x}+ C \\ & y \cdot \cot x=\log|\operatorname{cosec} x-\cot x|+\cos x+C \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the slope of the tangent to the curve at any point $\mathrm{P}(x, y)$ is $\frac{y}{x}-\cos ^{2} \frac{y}{x}$, then the equation of a curve passing through $\left(1, \frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is
questions.solution: According to the condition, $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\frac{y}{x}-\cos ^{2} \frac{y}{x} \ldots \text{ (i) }  This is a homogeneous differential equation Substituting $y=v x$, we get  \begin{array}{l} v+x \frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dx}}=v-\cos ^{2} v \\ \Rightarrow x \frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dx}}=-\cos ^{2} v \\ \Rightarrow \int \sec ^{2} \mathrm{vdv}=-\int \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{x}} \\ \Rightarrow \tan v=-\log x+\mathrm{C} \\ \Rightarrow \tan \frac{y}{x}+\log x=\mathrm{C} \end{array}$ Substituting $\mathrm{x}=1, y=\frac{\pi}{4}$, we get $\mathrm{C}=1$ Thus, we get $\tan \left(\frac{y}{x}\right)+\log x=1$ which is the required solution.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $The general solution of the differential equation \left(\tan ^{-1} y-x\right) d y=\left(1+y^{2}\right) d x$ is
questions.solution:
The given differential equation can be written as $\frac{d x}{d y}+\frac{x}{1+y^{2}}=\frac{\tan ^{-1} y}{1+y^{2}} \ldots$ (i)

Now, eq. (i) is a linear differential equation of the form $\frac{d x}{d y}+\mathrm{P}_{1} x=\mathrm{Q}_{1}$

where $\mathrm{P}_{1}=\frac{1}{1+y^{2}}$ and $\mathrm{Q}_{1}=\frac{\tan ^{-1} y}{1+y^{2}}$

Therefore, I.F $=e^{\int \frac{1}{1+y^{2}} d y}=e^{\tan ^{-1} y}$

Thus, the solution of the given differential equation is given by $x e^{\tan ^{-1} y}=\int\left(\frac{\tan ^{-1} y}{1+y^{2}}\right) e^{\tan ^{-1} y} \mathrm{dy}+\mathrm{C} \ldots$ (ii)

Let $\mathrm{I}=\int\left(\frac{\tan ^{-1} y}{1+y^{2}}\right) e^{\tan ^{-1} y} \mathrm{dy}$

On substituting $\tan ^{-1} y=t$, so that

$\left(\frac{1}{1+y^{2}}\right) \mathrm{dy}=\mathrm{dt}$, we get

$I=\int t e^{t} d t=t e^{t}-\int 1 \cdot e^{t} d t=t e^{t}-e^{t}=e^{t}(t-1)$ or $\mathrm{I}=e^{\tan ^{-1} y}   \left(\tan ^{-1}y-1\right)$

On substituting the value of 1 in equation (i1), we get

$x \cdote^{\tan ^{-1} y}=\cdote^{\tan ^{-1} y}\left(\tan ^{-1}$y-1\right)+  $\mathrm{C}or $x=$\left(\tan ^{-1}y-1\right)$+$\mathrm{C}  e^{$\tan ^{-1} y}

which is the general solution of the given differntial equation.

questions.solution: The given equation is $\frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{y}{x+1}=e^{3 x}(x+1)$ I.F. $=e^{\int-\frac{1}{x+1} d x}=e^{-\log (x+1)}=\frac{1}{x+1}$ The solution is $y\left(\frac{1}{x+1}\right)=\int e^{3 x}(x+1) \cdot \frac{1}{x+1} d x+a\Rightarrow \frac{y}{x+1}=\int e^{3 x} d x+a=\frac{e^{3 x}}{3}+a\Rightarrow \frac{3 y}{x+1}=e^{3 x}+c, c=3 a$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Solution of the equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{x - y}  \left(e^{x} - e^{y}\right) is$
questions.solution:
We have,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{x - y} \left(e^{x} - e^{y}\right)$

$⇒ $e^{y}$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + e^{y}e^{x} = e^{2x}$

Put $e^{y} = v$

$∴ $e^{y}$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dv}{dx}$

$∴ \dfrac{dv}{dx} + ve^{x} = e^{2x}$

This is linear equation

$I. F = = e^{∫ e^{x}dx} = e^{ex}$

$∴$ Required solution is

$v \cdote^{ex} = ∫ e^{ex} \cdote^{2x}dx + C$

$v \cdote^{ex} = e^{ex}\left(e^{x} - 1\right) + C$

$⇒ e^{y} \cdote^{ex} = e^{ex}\left(e^{x} - 1\right) + C$

$⇒ e^{y} = e^{x} - 1 + ce^{- e^{x}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f^{'}\left(x\right) = f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{0}^{1}f\left(x\right)dx, f\left(0\right) = 1$, then $f\left(x\right) =$
questions.solution:
Given,

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{0}^{1}f\left(x\right)dx, f\left(0\right) = 1... ( i )$

$⇒ f^{' '}\left(x\right) = f^{'}\left(x\right) + 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{f^{' '}\left(x\right)}{f^{'}\left(x\right)} = 1$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{f^{' '}\left(x\right)}{f^{'}\left(x\right)}dx = ∫ dx$

$⇒ logf^{'}\left(x\right) = x + C$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = Ae^{x}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = Ae^{x} + K$

$f\left(0\right) = A + K = 1... ( ii )$

$∴ Ae^{x} = Ae^{x} + K + {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(Ae^{x} + k\right)dx$

$⇒ k + {Ae^{x} + Kx}_{0}^{1} = 0$

$⇒ k + Ae - A + K = 0$

$⇒ A ( e - 1 ) + 2k = 0... ( iii )$

From Eqs. $( ii )$ and $( iii )$, we get

$A = \dfrac{2}{3 - e}, k = \dfrac{1 - e}{3 - e}$

$∴ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2e^{x}}{3 - e} + \dfrac{1 - e}{3 - e}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = sin  \left(x + y\right) + cos \left(x + y\right) is equal to$
questions.solution:
We have,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = sin\left(x + y\right) + cos\left(x + y\right)$

Put $x + y = v ⇒ 1 + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dv}{dx}$

$\dfrac{dv}{dx} - 1 = sinv + cosv$

$⇒ \dfrac{dv}{dx} = sinv + cosv + 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{dv}{sinv + cosv + 1} = dx$

$⇒ ∫ \left(\dfrac{1}{sinv + cosv + 1}\right)dv = ∫ dx$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{1}{\left\{\dfrac{2tan\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right)}{1 + {tan}^{2}\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right)}\right\} + \left\{\dfrac{1 - {tan}^{2}\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right)}{1 + {tan}^{2}\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right)}\right\} + 1}dv = ∫ dx$

$⇒ ∫ \left[\dfrac{\left\{1 + {tan}^{2}\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right)\right\}}{2tan\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right) + 1 - {tan}^{2}\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right) + 1 + {tan}^{2}\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right)}\right]dv = x + C$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left[\dfrac{{sec}^{2}\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right)}{tan\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right) + 1}\right]dv = x + C$

$⇒ log\left(tan\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right) + 1\right) = x + C$

$⇒ log\left(tan\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) + 1\right) = x + C$

questions.q: The equation of the curve whose slope at any point is equal to $y + 2x$ and which passes through the origin is
questions.solution:
We have, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y + 2x$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = 2x$

Now, $IF = e^{- ∫ 1dx} = e^{- x}$

$y \cdot e^{- x} = ∫ 2xe^{- x}dx + k, k$ be the constant of integration

$= 2\left[x ∫ e^{- x}dx - ∫ 1 \cdot \left(- e^{- x}\right)dx\right] + k$ [using integration by parts]

$⇒ y \cdot e^{- x} = - 2xe^{- x} - 2e^{- x} + k... \left(i\right)$

As curve (i) passes through $\left(0, 0\right)$

$∴ 0 = 0 - 2 + k$

$⇒ k = 2$

Thus, the curve is

$ye^{- x} = - 2xe^{- x} - 2e^{- x} + 2$

$∴ y = 2 \left(e^{x} - x - 1\right)

Hence, option (b) is correct.

$

questions.q: The solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = sin3x + e^{x} + x^{2}$ when ${y}_{1}\left(0\right) = 1$ and $y\left(0\right) = 0$, is
questions.solution:
Integrating the given differential equation, we have

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{- cos3x}{3} + e^{x} + \dfrac{x3}{3} + {C}_{1}$

But ${y}_{1}\left(0\right) = 1$

So, $1 = \left(- \dfrac{1}{3}\right) + 1 + {C}_{1}$

$⇒ {C}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$∴ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{- cos3x}{3} + e^{x} + \dfrac{x3}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3}$

Again integrating, we get

$y = - \dfrac{sin3x}{9} + e^{x} + \dfrac{x4}{12} + \dfrac{1}{3}x + {C}_{2}$

But $y\left(0\right) = 0,$ so $0 = 0 + 1 + {C}_{2}$

$⇒ {C}_{2} = - 1$

Thus, $y = - \dfrac{sin3x}{9} + e^{x} + \dfrac{x4}{12} + \dfrac{1}{3}x - 1$

Hence, option (a) correct.

questions.q: For any differentiable function $y$ of $x$, $\frac{d^{2} x}{d y^{2}}\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^{3}+\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=$
questions.solution: $\frac{d y}{d x}=\left(\frac{d x}{d y}\right)^{-1}\Rightarrow \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=-1\left(\frac{d x}{d y}\right)^{-2}\left\{\frac{d}{d x}\left(\frac{d x}{d y}\right)\right\}\Rightarrow \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=(-1)\left(\frac{d x}{d y}\right)^{-2}\left\{\frac{d}{d y}\left(\frac{d x}{d y}\right) \frac{d y}{d x}\right\}=(-1)\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^{2}\left\{\frac{d^{2} x}{d y^{2}} \cdot \frac{d y}{d x}\right\}=-\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^{3}\left\{\frac{d^{2} x}{d y^{2}}\right\}\Rightarrow \frac{d^{2} x}{d y^{2}}\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^{3}+\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\phi(\mathrm{x})$ is a differential function, then the solution of the differential equation $\mathrm{dy}+\left\{\mathrm{y} \phi^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})-\phi(\mathrm{x})\right.\left.\phi^{\prime}(x)\right\} d x=0,$ is
questions.solution: Given differential equation is $\mathrm{dy}+\left\{y \phi^{\prime}(x)-\phi(x) \phi^{\prime}(x)\right\} d x=0\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}+\phi^{\prime}(\mathrm{x}) \mathrm{y}=\phi(\mathrm{x}) \phi^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})$ which is a linear differential equation with $\quad P=\phi^{\prime}(x), Q=\phi(x) \cdot \phi^{\prime}(x)$ and $I \cdot F=e^{\int \phi^{\prime}(x) d x}=e^{\phi(x)}\therefore$ Solution is $y \cdot e^{\phi(x)}=\int \phi(x) \cdot \phi^{\prime}(x) e^{\phi(x)} d x+C\Rightarrow y \cdot e^{\phi(x)}=\int \phi(x) \cdot e^{\phi(x)} \phi^{\prime}(x) d x+C\Rightarrow y \cdot e^{\phi(x)}=\phi(x) e^{\phi(x)}-\int \phi^{\prime}(x) e^{\phi(x)} d x+C\Rightarrow y \cdot e^{\phi(x)}=\phi(x) e^{\phi(x)}-e^{\phi(x)}+C\Rightarrow y=\lceil\phi(x)-1]+C e^{-\phi(x)}$

questions.q: The solution to the differential equation $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y f^{\prime}(x)-y^{2}}{f(x)}$ where $f(x)$ is a given function is
questions.solution: We have $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)} y-\frac{y^{2}}{f(x)}\Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)} y=-\frac{y^{2}}{f(x)}$ Divide by $y^{2}: y^{-2} \frac{d y}{d x}-y^{-1} \frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)}=-\frac{1}{f(x)}$ Put $y^{-1}=z \Rightarrow-y^{-2} \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d z}{d x}-\frac{d z}{d x}-\frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)}(z)=-\frac{1}{f(x)}\Rightarrow \frac{d z}{d x}+\frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)} z=\frac{1}{f(x)}I F=e^{\int \frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)} d x}=e^{\log f(x)}=f(x)\therefore$ The solution is $z(f(x))=\int \frac{1}{f(x)}(f(x)) d x+c\Rightarrow y^{-1}(f(x))=x+c \Rightarrow f(x)=y(x+c)$
